 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. 49ers activate wide receiver Demarcus Robinson off IL after five-game absence originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area 
 Veteran wide receiver Demarcus Robinson appears set to resume his season.
 Meanwhile, Christian Kirk 's time with the 49ers might be over.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 49ers on Saturday made roster moves that impact the team's roster ahead of their Week 9 game Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium.
 Robinson was activated off the injured reserve list on Saturday after a five-game absence due to a high-ankle sprain he sustained in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins . Up to that point, Robinson had five catches for 84 yards and a touchdown.
 Robinson takes the roster spot that opened with Kirk being sidelined with a knee injury. The 49ers placed Kirk on injured reserve, and it could be a situation that prevents Kirk from playing for the 49ers for the remainder of the season.
 Kirk signed a one-year, $2.96 million contract in March. He sustained calf injuries early in the offseason program and again in training camp.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kirk made it onto the field for just one game, and the nine-year veteran was held without a catch in Week 7 while playing 20 snaps of offense against the Atlanta Falcons.
 The 49ers also elevated veteran receiver KhaDarel Hodge from the practice squad. Hodge serves as one of the team's top special-teams players. He was active for the first two games of the season before sustaining a knee injury. The 49ers released him with an injury settlement and re-signed him after he was healthy enough to play.
 On Friday, the 49ers ruled out Kirk, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring).
 Running back Christian McCaffrey , defensive end Nick Bosa and safety Marques Sigle were cleared to play against the Raiders. The 49ers' special teams should also get a boost with the returns of backup linebackers Luke Gifford and Garret Wallow.
